### [HIGH] SSRF

- **File:** `apps/web/lib/egress-policy.ts`
- **Line:** 74-81
- **Instance:** `isInternalHostname` IPv6 branch only rejects `::1`, `fc/fd` (ULA) and `fe8-b` (link-local) prefixes and returns `false` for everything else, so IPv4-mapped IPv6 literals like `::ffff:169.254.169.254` (and non-dotted IPv4 like decimal `2130706433`) are not normalized and are treated as public.
- **Risk:** A user-supplied image URL such as `https://[::ffff:169.254.169.254]/latest/meta-data/` passes `validateUserImageUrl`/`assertNonInternalHostname` (and `assertResolvedPublicHostname` early-returns at line 116 because `isIP` reports a valid IPv6), letting the provider image fetcher reach AWS IMDS / internal services — the exact SSRF amplification the module exists to prevent (WEB-MULTIMODAL-IMAGE-SSRF).
- **Fix:** Normalize IPv4-mapped/compatible IPv6 to their embedded IPv4 and re-run the IPv4 private/loopback checks, and reject non-dotted IPv4 notations (decimal/octal/hex) before allowing the host.

### [MEDIUM] BRITTLE FIX

### [MEDIUM] async race

- **File:** `apps/web/shared/lib/useCache.ts`
- **Line:** 25
- **Instance:** `fetchData` has no cancellation or stale-key guard, so when `key` changes mid-flight an older resolution can `setData` over the newer key's data; additionally `fetcher`/`tags` are typically new identities each render, recreating `fetchData` and re-running the effect (line 72) every render — a refetch loop.
- **Risk:** Stale data rendered under the wrong key plus unbounded refetch churn for non-memoized callers.
- **Fix:** Track a request epoch/AbortController per effect run and depend only on stable inputs.

### [MEDIUM] hardcoded success

- **Instance:** `checkSubscription` stub is hardcoded to return `{ allowed: true, hasAccess: true }` unconditionally, in a module whose header invites web code to import gate symbols from it.
- **Risk:** Any future web component that imports this gate (as the file's own docs instruct) gets a subscription check that always passes, silently disabling client-side gating of paid/waitlisted features.
- **Fix:** Make the stub fail closed (`allowed: false`) or remove the gate exports entirely so consumers are forced to use a real server-backed check.

### [MEDIUM] async race

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx`
- **Line:** 707
- **Instance:** The `initModels` effect re-runs on every `appMode` change with no cancellation/abort, so a slow in-flight run for the previous mode can resolve last and overwrite `useChatModelStore.setModels` after the user has switched modes.
- **Risk:** The model picker can display the prior mode's list (e.g., local/BYOK models while in managed-cloud mode, or vice versa), a stale trust-boundary-labeled UI state.
- **Fix:** Track a cancellation flag (or AbortController) in the effect and skip `setModels` when the captured mode no longer matches the current `appMode`.

### [LOW] response validation gap

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/App.tsx`
- **Line:** 718
- **Instance:** The web-mode fallback maps `/api/models` response items straight into the chat store with only an `Array.isArray` check — `id`/`name` are unvalidated and `provider` is cast to the ModelInfo provider union without the `validProviders` whitelist used on the primary path, and the fetch has no timeout.
- **Risk:** A malformed or slow API response yields undefined-labeled or arbitrarily-typed provider entries in the model picker and a hung fallback path.
- **Fix:** Validate each model object's fields (and reuse the provider whitelist) before `setModels`, and wrap the fetch with an AbortController timeout.

## Batch 115 — 20 files scanned

### [HIGH] contract drift

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/agent-collaboration/AgentCollaborationPanel.tsx`
- **Line:** 143
- **Instance:** Frontend listens for events `swarm:progress` (line 143), `swarm:agent_message` (line 150), and `swarm:complete` (line 169), but the Rust backend only emits `swarm:started`, `swarm:decomposed`, `swarm:completed`, `swarm:subtask_started/completed/failed` (src-tauri/src/core/swarm/orchestrator.rs:187-606), so none of these listeners ever fire.
- **Risk:** The agent list, agent-to-agent message feed, and swarm-complete result capture are permanently dead in production — the panel renders empty forever while a swarm actually runs.
- **Fix:** Align event names with the backend emits (or add the missing emits in orchestrator.rs) and add an integration test that asserts each listened event has a Rust fire site.

### [HIGH] API contract violation

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/agent-collaboration/AgentCollaborationPanel.tsx`
- **Line:** 198
- **Instance:** `invoke('swarm_init', { request: { maxAgents, autoSpawn, optimizeCriticalPath } })` sends camelCase keys, but Rust `SwarmInitRequest` (src-tauri/src/sys/commands/swarm.rs:30-35) declares snake_case fields `max_agents/auto_spawn/optimize_critical_path` with no `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`, so deserialization fails.
- **Risk:** The "Init Swarm" button always errors in the real desktop app, making the entire Agent Collaboration feature unusable.
- **Fix:** Add `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` to `SwarmInitRequest` (or send snake_case keys from the frontend) and cover the command with a round-trip test.

### [HIGH] contract drift

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/agent-collaboration/AgentCollaborationPanel.tsx`
- **Line:** 77
- **Instance:** The frontend `SwarmResult` interface expects camelCase `goalId/wallTime/speedupRatio/criticalPathLength/maxParallelism` with `wallTime` as a number, but Rust `SwarmResult` (orchestrator.rs:96-119) serializes snake_case fields and `wall_time` as a `Duration` struct (`{secs, nanos}`).
- **Risk:** Every results card renders "N/A"/undefined for wall time, speedup, parallelism, and critical path even on successful runs.
- **Fix:** Add `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` plus a millisecond serializer for `wall_time` on the Rust struct, or update the TS interface to the actual wire shape.

### [HIGH] contract drift

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/agent-collaboration/AgentCollaborationPanel.tsx`
- **Line:** 59
- **Instance:** Frontend `SwarmStats` expects `totalAgents/activeAgents/completedTasks/failedTasks/averageLatencyMs`, but Rust `SwarmStats` (orchestrator.rs:71-86) serializes `goals_processed/subtasks_created/subtasks_completed/subtasks_failed/peak_agents/avg_speedup_ratio/total_wall_time_ms` — zero overlapping field names.
- **Risk:** The stats bar (lines 797-807) renders "undefined completed / undefined failed / Avg latency: undefinedms" whenever stats load.
- **Fix:** Define a shared serde-camelCase stats DTO matching the TS interface and map the orchestrator fields into it.

### [HIGH] mock leakage

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/agent-collaboration/AgentCollaborationPanel.tsx`
- **Line:** 220
- **Instance:** `invoke('swarm_execute_goal', ...)` is not gated on `isTauri` (only the listeners are, line 132), and the shared `tauri-mock` shim returns `{ success: true, output: '(mock swarm result)' }` for this command in cloud-web/dev fallthrough (src/lib/tauri-mock.ts:1133-1140).
- **Risk:** In non-Tauri (cloud web) builds a user pressing Execute sees "Completed Successfully" with fabricated results while nothing actually ran — fake completion presented as real output.
- **Fix:** Gate the panel (or its invokes) on `isTauri` with an explicit "requires desktop app" state instead of letting mock success values render as results.

### [MEDIUM] implementation theater

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/agent-collaboration/AgentCollaborationPanel.tsx`
- **Line:** 268
- **Instance:** "Task delegation" to a specific agent is implemented by prefixing the goal string with `[Agent: ${agent.name}]` and calling the generic `swarm_execute_goal`, which spawns a fresh swarm goal rather than routing the task to the selected agent.
- **Risk:** The UI claims a task was assigned to a chosen agent while the backend ignores the selection, misleading users observing multi-agent workflows.
- **Fix:** Add a real backend command that targets a specific agent id (or remove the per-agent selector until it exists).

### [MEDIUM] lost update

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/agent-collaboration/AgentCollaborationPanel.tsx`
- **Line:** 274
- **Instance:** The `.then()` after `swarm_execute_goal` unconditionally sets the delegation status to `running`, but the invoke resolves only when the goal has finished, and it overwrites a `completed` status that the `swarm:agent_message` result handler (lines 155-163) may have set.
- **Risk:** Delegations are displayed as perpetually "running" after they finish, and a completed status can be regressed back to running.
- **Fix:** Set status to `running` before/immediately after dispatch and mark `completed` (guarding against status downgrades) when the invoke resolves.

### [MEDIUM] request validation gap

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/agent-collaboration/AgentCollaborationPanel.tsx`
- **Line:** 426
- **Instance:** The max-agents input uses `parseInt(e.target.value) || 5` without clamping to the declared 1-20 range (HTML `min`/`max` do not constrain typed values), and the value is sent straight to `swarm_init`.
- **Risk:** A typed value like 999 requests an unbounded agent swarm, risking resource exhaustion once the init contract bug is fixed.
- **Fix:** Clamp the parsed value to [1, 20] before storing it in state and validate `max_agents` server-side in the Rust command.

### [MEDIUM] hardcoded success

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/agi/AgentTaskMonitor.tsx`
- **Line:** 117-124
- **Instance:** `handleCancel` fires `toast.success('Task cancelled')` unconditionally after `await cancelTask(...)`, but the store's `cancelTask` (agentTaskStore.ts:441-459) swallows invoke errors internally and never rethrows, so the component's catch branch is dead and the success toast shows even when cancellation failed.
- **Risk:** User sees "Task cancelled" while the agent task is actually still running, contradicting the simultaneous store-level error toast and masking a failed cancel of an autonomous agent.
- **Fix:** Have the store rethrow (or return a boolean) from `cancelTask` and only toast success in the component when cancellation actually succeeded.

### [LOW] edge-case blindness

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/agi/AgentTaskMonitor.tsx`

- **Instance:** The 5-second auto-refresh effect only polls tasks with status `running`/`pending`, so tasks in the `paused`, `recovering`, or `expired` states defined in STATUS_CONFIG (lines 73-90) are never re-polled and their displayed status can stay frozen.
- **Risk:** A task that transitions out of `recovering`/`paused` in the backend keeps showing the stale state in the monitor until a full re-mount.
- **Fix:** Include `recovering` (and optionally `paused`) in the polling filter or subscribe to status-change events for those states.

### [HIGH] path traversal

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/artifacts/publishAdapter.ts`
- **Line:** 70
- **Instance:** The published file name interpolates `artifact.id` and the extension derived from `artifact.language` (line 50, `language ?? 'txt'`) without any sanitization, while only `artifact.title` is sanitized (line 69); `language` originates from LLM-generated artifact metadata and a value containing `/` or `..` (e.g. `ts/../../x`) redirects the `writeTextFile` target out of the `artifacts/` directory.
- **Risk:** LLM- or content-controlled path segments allow writing artifact content to arbitrary locations inside (or, depending on the Tauri fs scope, outside) the app data directory, overwriting app state or config files.
- **Fix:** Allowlist the extension (e.g. `/^[a-z0-9]{1,8}$/i`, else `txt`) and apply the same `[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]` sanitization to `artifact.id` before building the file name.

### [MEDIUM] Windows-path bug

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/artifacts/publishAdapter.ts`
- **Line:** 78
- **Instance:** Returns `` `file://${filePath}` `` by string concatenation while the comment on lines 75-77 claims "The URL constructor handles both cases correctly" — no URL constructor is used, so Windows paths produce invalid `file://C:\...` URLs and macOS app-data paths (which contain a space in "Application Support") produce URLs with unencoded spaces.
- **Risk:** Consumers that open or render the returned publish URL get a malformed file URL on Windows and macOS, breaking the local publish flow.
- **Fix:** Build the URL with proper conversion/encoding (e.g. `new URL('file:///' + filePath.replace(/\\/g, '/'))` with percent-encoding, or Tauri's path-to-URL helper) instead of raw concatenation.

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/artifacts/MarkdownArtifact.tsx`

- **Fix:** Replace raw palette classes with semantic token classes (e.g., text-primary/text-destructive) per the design-token rule.

- **Risk:** Every rendered diagram silently loses arrowheads and theme styling (and any htmlLabel content), shipping visibly broken diagrams while appearing to "work".
- **Fix:** Extend the allowlist with the Mermaid-required tags/attributes (`style`, `marker`, `marker-start/mid/end`, etc.) or sanitize with a DOMPurify SVG profile instead of a minimal hand-rolled list.

### [MEDIUM] security theater

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/artifacts/SvgArtifact.tsx`
- **Line:** 94
- **Instance:** Comment claims "Only allow href on elements that need it to prevent javascript: URI XSS", but the shared `sanitizeHtml` (apps/desktop/src/utils/security.ts:38-40) flattens the per-element `allowedAttributes` map into one global DOMPurify ALLOWED_ATTR array, so `href` is actually permitted on every allowed tag.
- **Risk:** The element-scoped href restriction the code documents does not exist; the only real protection is DOMPurify's default URI regexp, and any future change to ALLOW_UNKNOWN_PROTOCOLS or tag list silently widens the XSS surface believing scoping is in place.
- **Fix:** Implement true per-element attribute filtering (DOMPurify hook checking node.tagName) or correct the API/comment so callers know attribute scoping is global.

### [LOW] excessive data exposure

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/artifacts/SvgArtifact.tsx`

- **Instance:** `image` elements keep `href`, allowing untrusted artifact SVGs to reference remote http(s) images; currently blunted by the app CSP img-src allowlist (tauri.conf.json) but not by the sanitizer itself.

- **Fix:** Restrict image/use href values to data:/blob:/fragment URIs in the sanitizer rather than relying solely on CSP.

- **Instance:** The budget effect inspects only `messages[messages.length - 1]`; any message that completes or is appended in the same React batch as a newer message (e.g. a user message immediately followed by the assistant placeholder, or a still-streaming message that is no longer last when it finalizes) is never counted.

### [CRITICAL] tenant isolation failure

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/ChatInputArea.tsx`
- **Line:** 1051
- **Instance:** `handleSubmit` silently rewrites `providerOverride` to `'managed_cloud'` for any user on a managed plan whenever `selectedProvider !== 'ollama'`, which reroutes chats the user explicitly pointed at the local `lmstudio` provider (declared Local in `apps/desktop/src/types/provider.ts:18`) or at an explicit BYOK provider (anthropic/openai/etc.) into managed cloud with no consent flow, no payload preview, and no fork/continuation step.
- **Risk:** Local-only conversations and BYOK-keyed conversations are silently routed across the Local/BYOK/Managed-Cloud trust boundary — a direct violation of the locked product rule "Never silently route Local chats, files, or developer sessions to BYOK or managed cloud."
- **Fix:** Only apply the managed_cloud override when the user actually selected the managed_cloud/auto provider; exempt all local providers (`ollama`, `lmstudio`) and never override an explicit BYOK provider selection — route changes must go through the explicit fork/consent flow.

### [CRITICAL] tenant isolation failure

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/ChatInputArea.tsx`
- **Line:** 524
- **Instance:** `sendPendingMessage` (the queued-message auto-send path) duplicates the same silent override — `isManagedPlan && selectedProvider !== 'ollama' ? 'managed_cloud' : ...` — so queued messages composed against a local `lmstudio` or BYOK provider are auto-sent to managed cloud with zero user interaction at send time.
- **Risk:** Queued messages cross the Local/BYOK → Managed-Cloud trust boundary fully automatically (the user is not even present at the moment of send), leaking local-only content to the cloud backend.
- **Fix:** Share one provider-resolution helper that never overrides local or BYOK selections to managed_cloud without the explicit consent flow, and use it in both send paths.

### [HIGH] human-in-the-loop gap

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/ChatInputArea.tsx`
- **Line:** 840
- **Instance:** `detectAndCaptureScreen` regex-matches phrases like "what's on my screen" in the typed message and, on match (invoked from `handleSubmit` at line 932), auto-captures the full screen via `capture_screen_full` and sends it as an attachment in the same submit, with no confirmation or preview step before the capture leaves the machine.
- **Risk:** Screen contents (other apps, secrets, passwords, private messages visible on screen) are captured and uploaded to whatever provider the message routes to — including managed cloud via the line-1051 override — based solely on a text pattern, a PII-leakage path across trust boundaries without explicit user approval.
- **Fix:** Require an explicit user confirmation (or at minimum a visible pre-send preview with cancel) before auto-captured screenshots are attached and sent.

### [HIGH] insecure output handling

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/GenerativeWidget.tsx`
- **Line:** 49
- **Instance:** The CSP for LLM-generated widget HTML sets `connect-src 'none'` but allows `img-src data: https:` and `font-src https:`, so AI-authored markup can issue GET requests to arbitrary HTTPS hosts via `<img>`/`@font-face` URLs.
- **Risk:** Indirect prompt injection (e.g., poisoned web content in a prior tool result) can make the model emit a widget that exfiltrates conversation data to an attacker host through image-URL query strings — the classic markdown-image exfil channel this CSP otherwise tries to block.
- **Fix:** Restrict `img-src` to `data:` plus the same allow-listed CDN origins (and `font-src` likewise), or proxy remote images.

### [MEDIUM] message-validation gap

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/GenerativeWidget.tsx`
- **Line:** 144
- **Instance:** The comment claims "Only accept messages from our own blob URL origin" but `handleMessage` (lines 136-150) never checks `event.source`/`event.origin`, accepting any `widget-resize` message on the window.
- **Risk:** With multiple widgets rendered, every instance resizes on any widget's message (cross-talk), and any embedded frame can spoof resize messages to distort the chat layout; the comment is security theater.
- **Fix:** Accept only messages where `event.source === iframeRef.current?.contentWindow` and clamp height to a sane positive range.

### [CRITICAL] silent failure

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/index.tsx`
- **Line:** 357
- **Instance:** The SendPreview privacy banner computes `providerMode` from `selectedProvider` only (`!providerKey ? 'Local'`, lines 358-366), but the actual send path falls back to `llmConfig.defaultProvider` (lines 518-519, 902) — so with no explicit selection and a default provider of `managed_cloud` or a BYOK provider, the banner displays "Local" while the message is routed to cloud; per-send `options.providerOverride` is also never reflected in the banner.

- **Risk:** The user consents to a redacted, hash-attested payload preview (secret scan, "Redacted payload preview", SHA-256 hash) but the BYOK fork actually contains the full unredacted conversation history including any detected secrets — a Local-to-BYOK trust-boundary break where the consent artifact and the transmitted data diverge.
- **Fix:** Build the fork from the exact redacted payload/context items the user previewed (verifying against `previewHashSha256`), not from the raw conversation store.

### [HIGH] spec mismatch

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/LocalByokHandoffDialog.tsx`
- **Line:** 34-44
- **Instance:** The locked Local-to-BYOK rule requires explicit context selection, but `handoffContext` is hardcoded to `messages.slice(-20)` with no UI for the user to include/exclude messages, while the dialog still claims "N messages selected".
- **Risk:** Users cannot exclude sensitive messages from the handoff (their only option is cancel), and the "selected" wording misrepresents a hardcoded window, violating the consent contract for crossing the Local/BYOK boundary.
- **Fix:** Add a real per-message context selection step (checkbox list) feeding `selectedContext`, matching the locked handoff requirements.

### [HIGH] stale state

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/LocalByokHandoffDialog.tsx`
- **Line:** 86
- **Instance:** Creating a BYOK fork flips the GLOBAL `providerMode` to `'cloud'` via `setProviderMode('cloud')` (settingsStore `llmConfig.providerMode` is app-wide, not per-conversation), with nothing reverting it when the user returns to the original Local thread.
- **Risk:** After one BYOK fork, subsequent messages in unrelated Local conversations can route under cloud provider mode — contradicting the toast "The original Local thread is unchanged" and risking silent Local-to-BYOK routing.
- **Fix:** Scope provider mode to the forked conversation (per-conversation override) or restore the prior global mode when leaving the fork.

### [HIGH] approval-gate gap

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/MessageBubble/MessageBubble.tsx`
- **Line:** 372-388
- **Instance:** `pendingApprovalId` is resolved with `pendingApprovals.find(...)` that matches on tool NAME (`details['toolName']`/`details['tool']`) as readily as on the exact `actionId`, so the first pending approval for the same tool is bound to this message's ToolCallCard.
- **Risk:** With two concurrent pending approvals for the same tool (e.g., two shell commands), a message card can display and approve a different invocation's request — the user authorizes an action they never reviewed.
- **Fix:** Match strictly on `actionId` (or a per-invocation approval id) and only fall back to name matching when no actionId exists, never across multiple pending entries.

### [HIGH] insecure output handling

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/MessageBubble/ArtifactThumbnailCard.tsx`
- **Line:** 145-152
- **Instance:** LLM-generated artifact HTML (`artifact.content.slice(0, 800)`) is auto-rendered on message display in an iframe with `sandbox="allow-scripts"` and no CSP, so scripts in the artifact execute with zero user interaction.
- **Risk:** Indirect prompt injection (e.g., from a scraped web page) can make the model emit an artifact whose script/img beacons exfiltrate conversation-derived data over the network the moment the thumbnail renders — even in Local mode, defeating the local-privacy promise.
- **Fix:** Inject a restrictive CSP (`default-src 'none'`) into the srcDoc and/or render thumbnails as static screenshots, executing scripts only after explicit user interaction.

### [HIGH] unsafe deserialization

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/MessageBubble/MessageBubble.tsx`
- **Line:** 449-489
- **Instance:** Any completed tool result whose JSON contains an `__mcp_app` key is cast unvalidated to `McpAppContent` and auto-registered, then auto-rendered (lines 848-865) as an interactive scripted iframe app (McpAppRenderer: `allow-scripts allow-forms allow-popups`, card defaults to expanded) with no schema validation or user consent.
- **Risk:** A malicious or compromised tool/MCP server output gets zero-click script execution (network beacons, popups) inside the chat stream, and malformed payloads flow into the renderer unchecked.
- **Fix:** Validate the `__mcp_app` payload against a schema, restrict auto-render to allowlisted/approved MCP servers, and require user interaction before executing app scripts.

### [MEDIUM] insecure output handling

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/InlineToolResults/InlineVisionResult.tsx`
- **Line:** 52
- **Instance:** `imageUrl` taken from tool result data is rendered directly into `<img src={imageUrl}>` with no URL-scheme allowlist, while the sibling `InlineVoiceResult.tsx:67` validates `/^(https?:|data:|blob:)/i` before rendering its media URL.
- **Risk:** A tool result influenced by untrusted content (e.g., web pages the agent analyzed) can make the Tauri webview fetch arbitrary schemes such as `file://`/`asset://` paths, probing or rendering local files.
- **Fix:** Apply the same scheme allowlist used in `InlineVoiceResult` before assigning the image `src`.

### [MEDIUM] duplicate event handling

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/InlineToolResults/QuestionPrompt.tsx`
- **Line:** 33-43
- **Instance:** Every mounted `QuestionPrompt` subscribes globally to `question:ask` and adopts any incoming event as its own pending question without correlating `event.payload.id` to the component's tool invocation.
- **Risk:** With multiple `question` tool results in one conversation, several cards render the same interactive prompt (duplicate controls), and an older unanswered prompt is silently replaced by a newer unrelated question.
- **Fix:** Correlate the event payload `id` with the specific tool-call id this renderer instance owns and ignore non-matching events.

### [MEDIUM] silent failure

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/InlineToolResults/QuestionPrompt.tsx`
- **Line:** 69-76
- **Instance:** `handleSubmit` sets `submitted=true` and renders the "Answered" state before `agent.questionAnswer` resolves; on failure it only `console.error`s with no UI error or retry path.
- **Risk:** The user sees their answer as accepted while the backend never received it, so the waiting agent tool silently times out and the run stalls or fails confusingly.
- **Fix:** Surface the submission failure in the card (reset `submitted`, show an error with a retry button) instead of swallowing the rejection.

### [MEDIUM] duplicate event handling

- **Instance:** Every mounted `TodoList` subscribes globally to `todo:update` and replaces its local list with any payload, with no correlation id tying the event to the specific `todo_write` invocation this renderer represents.

- **Fix:** Include a tool-call/session correlation id in the `todo:update` payload and filter events to the owning invocation.

### [MEDIUM] filtering mismatch

- **Risk:** Users see assistant messages with content invisibly missing, which reads as model failure and hides requested output.

### [MEDIUM] semantic incorrectness

- **Line:** 61-72
- **Instance:** When no server-reported thinking duration exists, the fallback computes `Date.now() - message.timestamp`, which is time-since-message-creation, not thinking time, and it is recomputed on every render so the "Thought for Xs" label inflates as the message ages (any message under 1 hour old shows a growing bogus duration).

### [MEDIUM] context poisoning

### [MEDIUM] platform mismatch

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/ProjectSettingsDialog.tsx`
- **Line:** 334-340
- **Instance:** The drag-and-drop handler reads `(file as File & { path?: string }).path` — an Electron-only property that Tauri's webview does not expose — and falls back to the bare `file.name`, which is then passed to `file_read` as a filesystem path.

- **Fix:** Use Tauri's native drag-drop event (`onDragDropEvent`), which supplies real absolute paths, instead of HTML5 `dataTransfer.files`.

### [LOW] ARIA misuse

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/PromptSuggestionsDropdown.tsx`
- **Line:** 39
- **Instance:** `aria-expanded={isVisible}` is set on the `role="listbox"` popup container; `aria-expanded` belongs on the controlling element (the combobox/input), not the listbox itself.
- **Risk:** Screen readers receive an invalid attribute on the listbox role and the actual input never announces expanded state.
- **Fix:** Move `aria-expanded` (plus `aria-controls`/`role="combobox"`) onto the chat input that owns this dropdown and remove it from the listbox div.

### [MEDIUM] ignored promise

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/chat/RiskConfirmationDialog.tsx`
- **Line:** 93
- **Instance:** `useRiskConfirmation.confirm()` overwrites `resolveRef.current` on each call (line 94), so a second confirmation requested while one is pending leaves the first caller's Promise permanently unresolved; unmount while open also strands the pending Promise.
- **Risk:** Any tool/agent flow awaiting the first risk confirmation hangs forever (fails closed but deadlocks the operation) with no error.
- **Fix:** Resolve (or reject) the existing pending Promise with `false` before installing a new resolver, and resolve pending Promises on unmount.

### [MEDIUM] insecure output handling

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/editing/LivePreview.tsx`
- **Line:** 216
- **Instance:** `HtmlPreview` renders AI-modified HTML in an `srcDoc` iframe with `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-modals"` and no CSP, so remote resources (`img`, `style` URLs) load freely and any sanitizer bypass gets script execution.
- **Risk:** Prompt-injected pending HTML edits can exfiltrate data via remote resource fetches from a Local-only session, and `allow-scripts` removes a defense layer the sanitizer comment claims to provide.
- **Fix:** Drop `allow-scripts` (scripts are forbidden anyway) and inject a restrictive CSP meta into the srcDoc blocking remote loads.

### [MEDIUM] error-boundary gap

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/editing/LivePreview.tsx`
- **Line:** 149
- **Instance:** `PreviewRenderer` wraps its `return <ChildPreview/>` switch in try/catch, but React child render errors do not propagate through the parent's try/catch, so failures in MarkdownPreview/KaTeX/highlight rendering are uncatchable here.
- **Risk:** A malformed file (e.g. pathological math/markdown) crashes the whole panel instead of showing the designed "Preview Error" state.
- **Fix:** Wrap the preview content in a real React error boundary.

### [MEDIUM] stale state

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/editing/LivePreview.tsx`
- **Line:** 244
- **Instance:** `JsonPreview` calls `onError(...)` (a parent `setState`) synchronously during its own render when `JSON.parse` throws.
- **Risk:** "Cannot update a component while rendering a different component" warning and inconsistent error state in React 18 concurrent rendering.
- **Fix:** Parse in `useMemo` and report the error from a `useEffect`.

### [LOW] deprecated API usage

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/editing/VisualEditor.tsx`
- **Line:** 37
- **Instance:** Platform detection uses `navigator.platform`, which is deprecated.
- **Risk:** Future webview versions may return empty/frozen values, mislabeling shortcut hints.

### [HIGH] resource exhaustion

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/editor/MonacoEditor.tsx`
- **Line:** 361
- **Instance:** The create-editor effect depends on `options` (a `{}` default prop recreated every render, line 26) and `lsp` (useLSP returns a fresh object literal every render — useLSP.ts line 438), so the Monaco editor is disposed and fully recreated on essentially every re-render.
- **Risk:** Constant editor teardown/recreate loses cursor, scroll, selection, and undo state, churns LSP didOpen/didClose, and degrades performance badly in production.
- **Fix:** Memoize the options/LSP callbacks (stable identities) and key the effect on primitive deps only.

### [MEDIUM] ignored promise

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/editor/MonacoEditor.tsx`
- **Line:** 293
- **Instance:** `setInterval(updateDiagnostics, 1000)` polls an async function whose awaited `lsp.getDiagnostics` has no catch, producing an unhandled rejection every second while the LSP server is unhealthy.
- **Risk:** Rejection storms flood the console/error reporting and diagnostics silently stop updating.
- **Fix:** Wrap `updateDiagnostics` in try/catch and prefer event-driven diagnostics over 1s polling.

### [MEDIUM] Windows-path bug

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/editor/MonacoEditor.tsx`
- **Line:** 62
- **Instance:** File URI is built as `` `file://${filePath}` ``, which yields malformed URIs for Windows paths (`file://C:\...` instead of `file:///C:/...`).
- **Risk:** LSP didOpen/completions/hover silently fail on Windows builds because the server cannot resolve the document URI.
- **Fix:** Build the URI with a proper path-to-file-URL conversion (forward slashes, leading slash, percent-encoding).

### [MEDIUM] off-by-one error

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/editor/MonacoEditor.tsx`
- **Line:** 93
- **Instance:** Completion items use a zero-width range at the cursor (`startColumn === endColumn === position.column`), so accepting a suggestion inserts the full label without replacing the prefix the user already typed.
- **Risk:** Accepting "console" after typing "con" produces "conconsole" — completions are effectively broken.
- **Fix:** Compute the range from `model.getWordUntilPosition(position)`.

### [MEDIUM] hardcoded success

- **File:** `apps/desktop/src/features/error-handling/ErrorBoundary.tsx`
- **Line:** 104
- **Instance:** `componentDidCatch` fires `void errorReportingService.reportError(...)` and immediately sets `errorReported: true`, which renders "Error report sent successfully" (lines 195-204) before — and regardless of whether — the report actually succeeds.
- **Risk:** Users are told their crash report was sent when it may have failed, hiding error-reporting outages.
- **Fix:** Await the report (or `.then`) and only set `errorReported` on success.
